About

I am an aerospace engineer who graduated from IIT Kanpur in 2026. Over the last four years I have designed, built and tested rocket hardware: a solid rocket motor, a supersonic rocket, and a liquid engine.

I founded the IIT Kanpur rocket team, IITK RaSET, and led more than 50 students across propulsion, aerodynamics, structures and avionics. I then worked as a propulsion engineer at EtherealX on a semi-cryogenic liquid rocket engine, and today I am building Singularity Space Technologies.

I am also the founder of Singularity Space Technologies. We are building small and medium reusable launch vehicles that run on liquid methane and oxygen, with a first goal of a 50 kN Methalox engine and the test infrastructure to develop it. The aim is to make launch cheaper and give India a reusable rocket of its own.

Projects
2025 to 2026 · Project lead

India's first student-built supersonic rocket

I led aerodynamics and vehicle design for Prometheus. That meant nose-cone shape for low wave drag, compressible CFD in ANSYS Fluent, stability analysis across subsonic, transonic and supersonic flight, and fin design to avoid flutter. It flew to 3.3 km at about Mach 1.4.

3.3 km≈ Mach 1.4ANSYS Fluent6-DOF
2025 to now · Lead

Sagarmatha, a 7 kN liquid rocket engine

A bi-propellant engine with a 10 second burn time, the first high-power liquid rocket engine built by an Indian student team. I lead the design, with combustion analysis in NASA CEA, chamber and nozzle CFD, and 3D metal printing in Inconel.

7 kN10 s burnInconel 3D printingNASA CEA
2024 · Design, build, test

L-class solid rocket motor

India's most powerful student-built solid rocket motor, with 2,700 N peak thrust and 2,600 Ns total impulse. It has a reusable titanium and graphite nozzle and a Kapton thermal liner, both with patents filed. I also designed a 10 kN thrust stand and a dedicated launch stand for it.

2,700 N peak2,600 Ns10 kN stand2 patents filed

Singularity Space Technologies

Reusable Methalox rockets for small and medium payloads. Our first target is a 50 kN Methalox engine and a propulsion test facility, then a subscale reusable booster and landing demonstration.

MethaloxFull reuse500 kg and 5,000 kg to LEO
2026 · Built for Singularity Space

Singularity-Max, our own rocket engine design studio

A design suite for liquid rocket engines that runs in the browser. Give it a thrust, propellants and ambient pressure and it sizes a new engine: thermochemistry from NASA CEA, chamber and nozzle geometry, real flow, heat transfer with regenerative cooling, and wall stress analysis. The solver core is checked against NASA CEA2022 and published engine data. It is a conceptual design tool, not flight-hardware sign-off.

Spaceport America Cup 2024

Designed the aerodynamics of a fiberglass rocket aimed at 10,000 ft and Mach 0.9. Predicted apogee was 10,371 ft (3,166 m). The team qualified for the final stage among top student teams worldwide.

Teknofest 2025, Turkey

Led aerodynamic design and flight simulation for a high-power rocket targeting 3,259 m. Built the fiberglass body, nose cone and motor mount. IITK RaSET's first international competition qualification.
